text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and create human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. To get good results, users often practise "prompt engineering", which means writing clear instructions. LLMs can help with tasks like writing, translating, and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes, give outdated information, or repeat biases from their training data. They do not truly understand meaning like humans do, so checking their answers is always a good idea.
